title: FISH Signal Counting & Ratio Calculator
problem: Cytogenetic technologists manually count FISH signals across dozens of cells per case and calculate signal ratios to determine amplification, deletion, or translocation status. Manual counting is tedious, error-prone, and time-consuming, especially for cases requiring 200+ cell counts. Miscounts can lead to incorrect cancer diagnoses or missed abnormalities.
who: Cytogenetic technologists performing FISH analysis in oncology and prenatal labs

skill_spec.name: FISH Signal Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates FISH signal ratios, percentages of abnormal cells, and determines positive/negative cutoff status from raw cell counts
skill_spec.formula_hint: abnormal_pct = (abnormal_cells / total_cells) * 100; ratio = target_signals / reference_signals; positive if abnormal_pct > cutoff OR ratio > 2.0 for HER2

example_queries: I scored 200 cells for BCR/ABL: 185 showed 2R2G, 12 showed 1R1G1F, 3 showed 2R2G1F. Is this positive?
Calculate HER2 amplification ratio: 200 cells, total HER2 signals 890, total CEP17 signals 410

title: Culture Setup & Harvest Time Calculator
problem: Cytogenetic technologists must calculate precise culture setup times, mitotic arrest agent addition times, and harvest schedules for different specimen types (blood, bone marrow, amniotic fluid, solid tissue). Each specimen type requires different culture durations, media volumes, and synchronization protocols. Miscalculating timing leads to poor metaphase yields and repeat cultures, delaying critical diagnoses.
who: Cytogenetic technologists in hospital and reference cytogenetics labs

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetic Culture & Harvest Scheduler
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates optimal culture setup, colcemid addition, and harvest times based on specimen type and protocol

inputs.name: specimen_type
inputs.label: Specimen type (peripheral blood, bone marrow, amniotic fluid, CVS, tissue)

inputs.name: number_of_cultures
inputs.label: Number of cultures to set up

skill_spec.formula_hint: PHA blood=72h culture, colcemid 30min before harvest; bone marrow unstim=24h; amniotic fluid=7-10 days with feeding schedule; sync protocol adds thymidine block times

example_queries: I'm setting up a PHA-stimulated blood culture at 2pm today, when should I add colcemid and harvest?
Calculate harvest schedule for 3 bone marrow cultures: 1 direct, 1 unstimulated 24h, 1 synchronized

title: Karyotype ISCN Nomenclature Builder
problem: Writing karyotype descriptions using ISCN (International System for Cytogenomic Nomenclature) notation is complex and error-prone. Technologists must correctly describe chromosome number, sex chromosomes, structural and numerical abnormalities using strict formatting rules. Nomenclature errors in reports can cause misinterpretation by ordering physicians, leading to incorrect treatment decisions.
who: Cytogenetic technologists and lab supervisors writing karyotype reports

skill_spec.name: ISCN Karyotype Nomenclature Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Helps build correct ISCN notation for karyotype descriptions and validates existing nomenclature strings
skill_spec.expertise_area: ISCN 2024 cytogenomic nomenclature for constitutional and acquired abnormalities
context_needed: common abbreviations (del, dup, inv, t, der, add, mar)

example_queries: How do I write the ISCN for a male with a translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22 in 18 of 20 cells?
Is this nomenclature correct: 46,XX,del(5)(q13q33)[15]/46,XX[5]?
How do I describe a complex karyotype with 3 clones in a bone marrow sample?

title: CAP Accreditation Inspection Checklist
problem: CAP (College of American Pathologists) accreditation inspections require cytogenetics labs to demonstrate compliance across dozens of checklist requirements covering personnel qualifications, QC, proficiency testing, SOPs, and safety. Preparing for an inspection is stressful and time-consuming, and missing even one requirement can result in deficiencies that require corrective action or threaten accreditation.
who: Lab supervisors and managers preparing for CAP cytogenetics inspections

skill_spec.name: CAP Cytogenetics Inspection Prep Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Comprehensive pre-inspection checklist covering all CAP cytogenetics laboratory accreditation requirements
steps: Step 1: Verify all personnel qualifications and licensure are current (CG(ASCP) certification, state licenses)
Step 2: Confirm continuing education records are up to date for all staff
Step 3: Review and update all SOPs - ensure annual review signatures are current
Step 4: Verify QC records are complete for all reagents, stains, and media
Step 5: Confirm proficiency testing enrollment and results are documented (CAP surveys)
Step 6: Check instrument calibration and maintenance logs (microscopes, ovens, centrifuges)
Step 7: Verify specimen tracking - accession to final report chain of custody
Step 8: Review turnaround time compliance data
Step 9: Confirm safety documentation (chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance)
Step 10: Audit recent karyotype and FISH reports for nomenclature accuracy
Step 11: Verify competency assessment records for all technical staff
Step 12: Check corrective action documentation for any previous deficiencies
warnings: Warning: All SOPs must have documented annual review even if no changes were made
Warning: Proficiency testing failures require documented root cause analysis and corrective action
Warning: Personnel who have not completed required CE hours cannot perform testing

example_queries: We have a CAP inspection next month, what do I need to prepare for cytogenetics?
What are the most common CAP deficiencies in cytogenetics labs?

title: QC Documentation & Levy-Jennings Tracker
problem: Cytogenetic technologists must document daily quality control for reagents, stains, culture media, and probe performance. Tracking QC trends over time using Levy-Jennings charts is required for CAP/CLIA compliance but is often done manually in spreadsheets, which is tedious and makes it hard to spot out-of-range trends before they cause testing failures.
who: Cytogenetic technologists responsible for daily QC and lab supervisors reviewing QC data

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetics QC Trend Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates QC statistics, detects Westgard rule violations, and tracks reagent/probe performance trends

inputs.name: qc_parameter
inputs.label: QC parameter (e.g., band resolution, FISH signal intensity, mitotic index)

inputs.name: values
inputs.label: QC values (comma-separated, most recent 20-30 data points)

skill_spec.formula_hint: mean = sum(values)/n; SD = sqrt(sum((x-mean)^2)/(n-1)); CV = (SD/mean)*100; Westgard rules: 1-2s warning, 1-3s reject, 2-2s reject, R-4s reject, 4-1s reject, 10x reject

example_queries: Check these QC values for Westgard violations: 98, 101, 99, 103, 97, 105, 108, 110, 112, 109
Calculate mean and SD for my FISH probe signal intensity QC data from the last month

title: Karyotype Analysis Report Generator
problem: Cytogenetic technologists prepare detailed karyotype analysis reports for each patient case, including clinical indication, specimen information, methodology, results in ISCN notation, and interpretive comments. Writing these reports is repetitive and time-consuming, especially for common abnormalities where standard interpretive language exists. Inconsistent report language across technologists can confuse clinicians.
who: Cytogenetic technologists and lab supervisors preparing final reports

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetic Report Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates standardized karyotype and FISH analysis reports with appropriate interpretive comments based on findings

variables.name: specimen_type
variables.label: Specimen type (blood, bone marrow, amniotic fluid)

variables.name: abnormality_type
variables.label: Abnormality type (normal, trisomy, translocation, deletion, etc.)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (lab info, patient info) -> Clinical Indication -> Specimen Info -> Methodology -> Results (ISCN) -> Interpretation -> Recommendation for follow-up testing if applicable -> Technologist/Director signatures

example_queries: Generate a karyotype report for a bone marrow sample showing Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) in a CML patient
Write a FISH report for prenatal trisomy 21 detected in amniotic fluid

title: ASCP Continuing Education Tracker
problem: Cytogenetic technologists with CG(ASCP) certification must complete continuing education credits within specific timeframes and categories to maintain certification. Tracking credits across multiple providers, ensuring category requirements are met, and calculating remaining credits needed before the deadline is confusing and often done last-minute, risking certification lapse.

skill_spec.name: ASCP CE Credit Tracker
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates remaining CE credits needed for CG(ASCP) certification maintenance by category and deadline

inputs.name: credits_earned
inputs.label: Credits earned by category (e.g., cytogenetics=12, general lab=6, safety=2)

inputs.name: total_required
inputs.label: Total CE credits required for cycle

outputs.name: credits_per_month
outputs.label: Credits needed per remaining month to stay on track

skill_spec.formula_hint: remaining = required - earned; months_left = deadline - today in months; pace = remaining / months_left; check each category meets minimum

I have 20 cytogenetics credits and 4 safety credits. Am I meeting ASCP category requirements?

title: Chromosome Abnormality & Clinical Significance Reference
problem: Cytogenetic technologists encounter a wide variety of chromosomal abnormalities and must quickly determine their clinical significance for report interpretation. Technologists need to look up whether a specific translocation, deletion, or gain is associated with a particular cancer subtype, syndrome, or is a normal variant. This information is scattered across multiple databases and textbooks.
who: Cytogenetic technologists interpreting karyotypes and FISH results

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetic Abnormality Clinical Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of chromosome abnormalities, associated diseases/syndromes, genes involved, and clinical significance
skill_spec.data_domain: Recurrent chromosome abnormalities in cancer and constitutional genetics, WHO classification of hematologic neoplasms

title: Specimen Rejection Criteria Advisor
problem: Cytogenetic technologists must evaluate incoming specimens to determine if they meet acceptance criteria for testing. Decisions about whether to reject, accept with disclaimer, or request a recollect depend on specimen type, transport conditions, age, volume, and clinical urgency. Incorrect rejection of a critical specimen delays diagnosis; accepting a poor specimen wastes resources and may produce unreliable results.
who: Cytogenetic technologists receiving and accessioning specimens

skill_spec.name: Specimen Acceptance/Rejection Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Advises on specimen acceptability for cytogenetic testing based on type, condition, transport, and clinical urgency
skill_spec.expertise_area: Cytogenetic specimen requirements, rejection criteria, and exception handling for urgent cases

example_queries: Bone marrow arrived 36 hours after collection in sodium heparin, room temp. Can I still culture it?
Amniotic fluid sample is blood-tinged and only 8mL. Should I reject or try to set up?
Blood for karyotype came in EDTA instead of heparin. Can I use it?

title: Troubleshooting Failed Cultures & Poor Preparations
problem: When cell cultures fail to grow, metaphase spreads are poor quality, or banding is suboptimal, technologists must diagnose the root cause and determine corrective action. Troubleshooting involves evaluating multiple variables (media, temperature, reagents, technique) and the knowledge is often tribal, learned through years of experience. Failed cultures delay critical diagnoses.
who: Cytogenetic technologists dealing with culture failures or poor slide quality

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetics Troubleshooting Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Systematic troubleshooting guide for failed cultures, poor metaphases, suboptimal banding, and FISH failures
steps: Step 1: Identify the problem category (no growth, poor mitotic index, poor morphology, poor banding, FISH failure)
Step 2: For no growth - check specimen viability (collection time, transport), media QC, incubator temp/CO2, contamination
Step 3: For low mitotic index - verify colcemid concentration and exposure time, check culture duration, evaluate cell density
Step 4: For poor chromosome morphology - evaluate hypotonic treatment time and temperature, fixation technique, humidity during spreading
Step 5: For poor banding - check trypsin age/concentration, Giemsa stain preparation, slide aging time, destaining if needed
Step 6: For FISH failure - verify probe hybridization conditions, check denaturation temperature, evaluate slide pretreatment
Step 7: Review QC records for reagent lot changes or equipment issues
Step 8: Document troubleshooting steps and corrective action taken
Step 9: Determine if specimen recollection is needed and communicate to ordering physician
warnings: Warning: Always save remaining specimen material before troubleshooting in case recollection is not possible
Warning: Document all troubleshooting for CLIA/CAP compliance
Warning: For oncology specimens, prioritize FISH on direct preparations if culture fails
regulatory_refs: CAP CYG checklist - corrective action requirements

example_queries: My bone marrow culture has no metaphases after 24 hours. What should I check?
G-banding looks washed out on today's slides. How do I troubleshoot?
FISH signals are very faint and background is high. What went wrong?

title: Turnaround Time Compliance Monitor
problem: Cytogenetics labs must meet turnaround time (TAT) targets for different test types - STAT FISH within 24 hours, routine FISH 48-72 hours, karyotypes 7-14 days. Tracking compliance across multiple specimen types and test categories is complex, and TAT failures can trigger CAP deficiencies, affect patient care, and require documented corrective action plans.
who: Lab supervisors and managers responsible for TAT compliance reporting

skill_spec.name: Cytogenetics TAT Compliance Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates turnaround time compliance rates by test type and identifies cases exceeding target TAT

inputs.name: test_type
inputs.label: Test type (STAT FISH, routine FISH, karyotype, prenatal)

inputs.name: cases_data
inputs.label: Case data: received date/time and reported date/time pairs

inputs.name: target_tat_hours
inputs.label: Target TAT in hours for this test type

outputs.name: outliers
outputs.label: Cases exceeding target TAT with details

skill_spec.formula_hint: TAT = report_datetime - received_datetime; compliance_rate = (cases_within_target / total_cases) * 100; flag outliers > 1.5x target

example_queries: Calculate our FISH TAT compliance for this month: 45 cases, 42 reported within 48 hours, 3 took 72+ hours
What is our average karyotype turnaround time if these are my case TATs: 8, 10, 9, 14, 11, 7, 12, 15, 9, 10 days?
